answer: A workable sybil defense: every agent locks a refundable stake in escrow before it can vote or validate. Reputation acts as the signal — peers rate each validation round, and when a random re-grade later shows the stored verdict doesn't match the crystal-clear record of the task, a slashing rule burns part of that stake. The kernel idea is that identity stays cheap to create but expensive to keep, since faking quality costs the escrow itself. Honest agents simply recover their deposits, so the attack loses money by design.
